traits.bark_colour.note: The bark colour chosen by eye for appearance (see its note), as a screen colour: it stood as appearance.bark [0.33, 0.15, 0.1], which is linear light, so the trunk drew pale grey to white beside photographs of the species (2026-10-23). It stands here in sRGB, as bark colours are picked, and the bark rule (tracheophyta) turns it into linear light.

traits.limb_angle.note: Sargent's Manual (sargent-1922, p. 572): 'slender rather upright branches forming a symmetric oblong head'.

traits.shade_tolerance.note: FEIS's bitter cherry review (Prunus emarginata, read 2026-10-16): "a generally shade intolerant species of sparse woods".

traits.flowering_months.note: FEIS (Prunus emarginata): April to June in British Columbia. Too few iNaturalist records in the Puget Sound lowlands are annotated as flowering to count (22).

traits.fruiting_months.note: FEIS (Prunus emarginata): ripe from July to September, its seed dispersed in August and September.

traits.wood_density_basic_kg_m3.note: GWDD v.2.2 species aggregate for Prunus emarginata (gwddagg_v2.2_species.csv, read): specific gravity 0.49 (wsg_est, the database's hierarchical-model species mean, from 1 record in 1 source); trunks 0.49, branches 0.54. Basic density (oven-dry mass over green volume) is the specific gravity times 1000 kg/m3.

generator.params.path_half.note: A choice of the model's (crown form step B, broadleaf revision 11): the wood from the base at which a shoot's nodes are half as long, fitted so the plant grows to the height of its oldest reference size, with the crown's width left to grow inside the loose region.

generator.params.note: Hand-set from general knowledge of the species: a slender tree with a narrow crown, alternate oblong, finely toothed leaves and small clusters of white flowers. Not fitted to measurements. Its crown's width is the broadleaf trees' rule from the measured width over height of open-grown trees of its lineage (crown_spread, USDA Urban Tree Database) since 2026-10-23, in place of a hand-set crown_radius. Its crown's base is the broadleaf trees' rule from the measured share of the tree's height below its crown (crown_base_share, USDA Urban Tree Database), and its stem divides only where its flora or photographs say its leader is lost or that it stands on several stems, since 2026-10-24, in place of hand-set crown_base and fork values.

allometry.note: The USDA Urban Tree Database's open-grown cherries in the Pacific Northwest region (McPherson, van Doorn and Peper 2016, RDS-2016-0005; Longview), since it has no bitter cherries: 39 cherry plums and Japanese flowering cherries 25 to 35 years old, median 10.0 m tall and 48 cm through, read as 30 years. Was 12 m and 22 cm at 30 years, from general knowledge.

appearance.note: Colours chosen by eye: green leaves; smooth, shiny reddish-brown bark. Fruit (plant roadmap P4), as in mid-July: corymbs of bright red cherries about 1 cm across, a few still green. Its year (appearance.organs.bloom.season) takes its days of bud, flower, fruit, ripe and fall from the months it flowers and fruits in, by the rules at the flowering plants (development, 2026-10-14); until then they were authored from general knowledge of the species in the south Puget Sound lowlands: white flowers in April and May; cherries red in July, gone by early September. The forest's packages show day 196 (mid-July) until the phenology of plant roadmap P5 sets the day from the date and the local climate. Bark pattern (plant roadmap P4, `bark_pattern`): smooth reddish-brown bark with prominent horizontal lenticels; set from general knowledge of the species, not measured. Leaf families (plant roadmap P4, `families`): sun leaves a little smaller and narrower than shade leaves; set from general knowledge of sun and shade leaves and juvenile foliage, not measured.

taxon.note: Scientific and common names (and USDA symbol, where given) as the spec's authors wrote them, and the genus the scientific name is written in.

growth_form.note: The growth form the spec's authors chose from the plant's habit.

growth.note: The growth plan (years, step, keyframes) chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

variants.note: The environments, conditions and seeds chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

taxon.family.note: WCVP v16's family for the accepted name.

taxon.plant_name_id.note: WCVP v16's plant_name_id for the accepted species the name resolves to (the accepted name).

appearance.organs.bloom.season.flower_lo.note: Its flowers drawn one by one (spec rework L1b): white flowers 10 to 15 mm across with notched petals and about 20 stamens, in small flat clusters that open together. From general descriptions of the species (OregonFlora, the Flora of North America and nursery and extension pages as quoted in search results; the pages themselves were not read). The size is the flower's width, or a closed corolla's length, over the fruit's length, roughly as in life. Its flower laid out whorl by whorl (spec rework P5b): five white petals between five sepals on a floral cup, about twenty stamens and one pistil, from the characters of Rosaceae and Prunus by the rules at the flowering plants.
